newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S., France agree on Bildt successor for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S., France agree on Bildt successor for Bosnia.

text.p: The United States and France have agreed that Carlos Westendorp, Spain's ambassador to the United Nations, should be the next international envoy to Bosnia, diplomatic sources said Monday.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, after talks with her French counterpart, acknowledged agreement on the issue but refused to identify the individual. However, diplomatic sources told Reuters: "Westendorp is right."

The United States has been pushing for American Jacques Klein, U.N. administrator for the difficult situation in Croatia's disputed eastern Slavonia region, to be Westendorp's deputy and officials said a consensus was forming around that appointment.
They said, though, that a second deputy may be named and that a European would fill that role.

The major western powers involved in Bosnia peace efforts -- the United States, France, Germany, Russia and Britain -- were expected to appoint Westendorp during a meeting on Friday in Sintra, Portugal. He would succeed Swedish diplomat Carl Bildt who for months has delayed leaving the post because the major powers could not agree on a replacement.

One of Albright's main goals on a week-long trip to Europe, including the Balkans, is to push a U.S. initiative for more aggressive peace efforts in Bosnia. The U.S.-brokered Dayton peace accords ended war there but there are increasing concerns that efforts to secure the peace by building a unified Bosnia are foundering because of lingering hostilities among rival factions, resistance to integration and lack of cooperation in bringing war criminals to trial.
